newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan hails Annan's appointment as U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Japan hails Annan's appointment as U.N. chief.

text.p: Japan welcomed on Wednesday the formal appointment of Kofi Annan as new U.N. secretary-general.
"Japan heartily welcomes the appointment of the present undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations as new U.N. secretary-general," Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said in a statement.
The General Assembly on Tuesday appointed Annan, a 58-year-old U.N. career official from Ghana, by acclamation to a five-year term as U.N. secretary-general, beginning on January 1.
Annan will be the seventh secretary-general in the history of the 51-year-old organisation and the first from sub-Saharan Africa.
Ikeda said Japan would closely cooperate with Annan in an effort to ensure global peace and prosperity.
Annan succeeds Egyptian Boutros Boutros-Ghali, 74, who was the first secretary-general from the African continent.
"We would like to thank present secretary-general Boutros-Ghali...for his great contribution in the international arena these past five years," Ikeda said.
The United States blocked Boutros-Ghali's hopes for a second term, saying he had not done enough to carry out reforms and that the world organisation needed new leadership.
